Definition: from G2556; badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble:--evil, malice(-iousness), naughtiness, wickedness.
BiblicalUsage: Kakia is badness itself — depravity in the heart, malice in the hand. Jesus says sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof; Paul says let all bitterness and wrath and clamour and evil speaking be put away from you, with all malice; Peter says lay aside all malice and all guile; and James says receive with meekness the engrafted word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe malice is not a mood but a weight to be laid aside. Scripture never tells me to manage it or excuse it — it tells me to put it off, and the engrafted word is what takes its place.
